land.text: Hesse, split from Thuringia in the War of the Thuringian Succession: 'Partitioned from Duchy of Thuringia: 1264'

predecessors.note: The Thuringian dossier of eu-08-x ends 1264; Meissen kept Thuringia.

land.text: 'His eldest son William IV inherited the northern half of the Landgraviate and the capital of Kassel' (Hesse-Kassel page)
George, the youngest son, 'received the Hessian lands in the former upper County of Katzenelnbogen' (Hesse-Darmstadt page)
Upper Hesse round Marburg, Louis IV's share
the lower County of Katzenelnbogen on the Middle Rhine, Philip II's share

capitals.name: Marburg
capitals.note: The infobox lists 'Marburg, Gudensberg, Kassel (from 1277)' without years for the first two; the span is an inference (confidence 1).

rulers.name: Henry I the Child
rulers.note: Infobox 'First landgrave'; 'raised to the status of prince by King Adolf of Germany in 1292'. Only the first and the last landgrave are on the page.

rulers.name: Philip I the Magnanimous
rulers.note: Infobox 'Last landgrave'; Protestant after the 1526 Synod of Homberg.

correction.text: Lower Hesse round Kassel and Upper Hesse round Marburg and Giessen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row (the lands are in 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States'). The page names Marburg, Gudensberg and Kassel as seats and Upper and Lower Hesse as the two halves but gives no boundary or area; radius reading, soft.

correction.text: Hesse with the Upper County of Katzenelnbogen round Darmstadt and the lower county on the Middle Rhine

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Katzenelnbogen male line died out in 1479 and 'The Obergrafschaft was passed to the Landgraves of Hesse'; the lower county's passage is not stated but Hesse-Rheinfels existed in 1567 (Landgraviate of Hesse page).

ledger.note: 1264: Henry I the Child becomes the first Landgrave of Hesse. 'In 1264 he became the first Landgrave of Hesse and the founder of the House of Hesse'; infobox 'Partitioned from Duchy of Thuringia: 1264'. The War of the Thuringian Succession page: 'the war secured his Hessian possessions'.

region.text: Lower Hesse round Kassel and Upper Hesse round Marburg and Giessen

ledger.note: 1308: Hesse is divided into Upper and Lower Hesse until 1311. 'From 1308 to 1311, and again from 1458, the landgraviate was divided into Upper Hesse and Lower Hesse.'
1311: the two halves are joined again (end of the first division).
1458: the second division into Upper and Lower Hesse begins (to 1500).

1479: the Upper County of Katzenelnbogen comes to Hesse. 'When Philipp died in 1479, the male line of the Katzenelnbogens became extinct. The Obergrafschaft was passed to the Landgraves of Hesse by virtue of the 1458 marriage of Henry III of Upper Hesse to Count Philipp's daughter Anna'; the upper county 'lay south of the Main River around Darmstadt'. The lower county on the Middle Rhine is not said to pass.

region.text: the Obergrafschaft south of the Main round Darmstadt, and the Untergrafschaft on the Middle Rhine

ledger.note: 1500: Hesse is re-united. 'Hesse was re-unified under Landgrave William II in 1500.'

1567: Hesse is divided among four sons. 'When Philip I died in 1567, Hesse was divided between his sons from his first marriage': Hesse-Kassel to William IV, Hesse-Marburg to Louis IV, Hesse-Rheinfels to Philip II, Hesse-Darmstadt to George I.
1567: the Landgraviate of Hesse ends in the four-way partition; the Rheinfels line dies out in 1583 and the Marburg line in 1604, both 'incorporated into Hesse-Kassel' (and Darmstadt for Marburg).

wars.name: War of the Thuringian Succession

zones.text: Hesse, claimed by Sophie of Brabant for her son against the Archbishop of Mainz, who said 'Hesse was a fiefdom of the Archbishopric'

wars.outcome: Brabant keeps Hesse ('This created the Landgraviate of Hesse'); the Margrave of Meissen takes Thuringia and the title of Landgrave of Thuringia.
wars.note: 'The war lasted over 17 years' from Henry Raspe's death in 1247; the page gives no treaty date, so the end year 1264 comes from the Landgraviate of Hesse page.

certainty.note: The page names seats and the Upper/Lower division, no boundaries; the Katzenelnbogen lands were detached enclaves.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages opened; page budget 2-5). New state: Cliopatria lacks Hesse before 1803 (its lands are in 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States').

SHAPES ARE RADIUS READINGS: Kassel 55 km, Marburg (8.77E 50.81N) 40 km, Giessen 40 km, Darmstadt (8.65E 49.87N) 30 km, St. Goar/Rheinfels (7.71E 50.15N) 14 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Marburg', 'Darmstadt', 'St. Goar', 'Katzenelnbogen' (places).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page gives no area and no year for the end of the Thuringian war (the 1264 date is the infobox's). (2) 1292 (prince status), the Reformation (1526 Synod of Homberg) and Philip's reign are not territorial. (3) The Schmalkaldic War and Philip's capture in 1547 are not on the page. (4) The lower county of Katzenelnbogen is not said to pass to Hesse in 1479 on the Katzenelnbogen page; the keyframe includes it because Hesse-Rheinfels existed in 1567. (5) Nassau-Siegen disputed the inheritance 1500-1557 (Katzenelnbogen page). (6) Rulers: only Henry I and Philip I are given by the page.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: landgraviate-of-hesse-marburg (1567-1604), landgraviate-of-hesse-rheinfels (1567-1583), county-of-katzenelnbogen (1095/1138-1479), plus Hesse-Kassel and Hesse-Darmstadt, written in this batch.
